directions.thesis: Reproduce the legacy page: title over an honest response-time line, then two columns - channels and the founder card on the left, the message form on the right.
tradeoffs: Two columns compete: a tall form owns half the screen even though most readers came to tap one channel.
On mobile the form falls to the very bottom, below four channels and a founder card.
legacyDivergence: The contact FAQ is dropped - out of the scope the owner set.
Zalo is added to the channel list; it exists in neither repository.
GitHub is removed from the founder socials.
For a signed-in viewer the form card becomes a founder DM entry.

directions.thesis: The page answers 'who are you' before anything else. Four channels sit in a compact strip; below them is ONE conversation surface - a guest sees the form, a signed-in learner sees their founder DM thread with its history. The session decides which door exists, so two of them never compete for the same screen.
directions.primaryCta: Gui tin - its shape decided by the session
tradeoffs: The most expensive direction: the most new owners, the most states, and a thread that must learn about replies in a codebase with no messaging convention to inherit.
A learner who is signed in never sees the guest form, so a bug in either branch hides from half the readers.
The channel strip demotes email and Zalo to equal weight, which a reader in a hurry may read as four equally slow options.
legacyDivergence: The two-column grid is replaced by a strip over a single panel.
The founder card stops being a separate card and becomes the conversation's own header identity.
GitHub is removed; Zalo is added.
The signed-in reader gets a durable conversation, which the legacy page had no equivalent of.

directions.thesis: The channels ARE the page. Four large rows, each showing its real handle so the reader knows the destination before tapping. The founder becomes an identity row under the title rather than a card, and the form collapses into a disclosure at the end for readers who use none of the four.
tradeoffs: The form is hidden behind one press, so a reader who genuinely needs to write a long message must open it first.
It demotes the form relative to legacy, and fewer written messages is a cost that only shows up after release.
legacyDivergence: The founder card becomes an identity row.
The contact FAQ is dropped; GitHub removed; Zalo added.

blockTrees.note: One channel: its glyph, its name, and the real handle it leads to. Pressable, external, opens in a new tab.
The guest door. Owns the four controls, their refusals, and the submitted state.
The signed-in door. Owns the thread, its ordering, and the pending-message state.

contracts.why: Exactly one of the two doors exists at a time, so both are optional slots rather than one slot holding null - the same rule the catalog's owned and discover groups follow.
Four peers of equal weight read as a row of choices; the same four stacked would read as a ranking nobody decided.
The handle is shown rather than hidden behind the name, because a reader decides whether to tap by recognising the destination - an unlabelled Facebook tile asks them to trust it instead.
A thread is read newest-last, so its own order is the content; nothing above it may re-sort it.
Already owns 'where the reader is, above what this page is'. The catalog reached for it and so does this.
The entry already owns the label-control-hint relationship; what it does not yet admit is a control that is not one line. Without this, no form on this page can be expressed at all.

vocabularyProposals.meaning: A multi-line box for prose the reader writes themselves.
vocabularyProposals.api: LeafProps<{ id, name, label, placeholder?, defaultValue?, rows?, isInvalid?, disabled? }, { change?: (value: string) => void }>
vocabularyProposals.notAProp: Input owns a one-line well with a reveal affordance. A resizable multi-line box is a different visual slot, so extending InputKind would rename a different control rather than reuse the same one.
tests: renders the label pointing at the box
keeps typed text across a re-render

vocabularyProposals.meaning: One choice from a short closed set, chosen from a popover list.
vocabularyProposals.api: LeafProps<{ id, name, label, options: ReadonlyArray<{ id, label }>, selectedKey?, placeholder?, isInvalid?, disabled? }, { select?: (id: string) => void }>
vocabularyProposals.vendor: HeroUI Select.Root / Trigger / Value / Indicator / Popover with ListBox.Root, which is what the legacy form already uses.
vocabularyProposals.notAProp: ChoiceTabs shows every option at once and switches a panel; a select hides its options and fills a field. Same data, different promise.
tests: renders the placeholder when nothing is chosen

vocabularyProposals.meaning: One message in a conversation, and whose it is.
vocabularyProposals.api: LeafProps<{ content: string, author: "viewer" | "other", timeLabel: string, status?: "sent" | "pending" | "failed" }, { retry?: () => void }>
tests: sides the viewer's own message opposite the other's
marks a failed message and offers retry
never drops the text of a failed message

vocabularyProposals.meaning: The box a reply is written in, together with the act of sending it.
vocabularyProposals.api: { props: { placeholder, sendLabel, isSending? }, on: { send?: (text: string) => void } }
vocabularyProposals.why: The box and its send button are one act, not two neighbours - the seam between them belongs to whoever owns both.
